item.title: Building an Automated Open Source Management Environment: cdxgen + Dependency-Track
item.description:
For companies just starting with open source management, we recommend the cdxgen + Dependency-Track combination as a toolset that can establish a basic automation environment within a single day.

This guide walks you through every step, from installation and configuration to setting up a license and vulnerability inspection environment and running day-to-day operations.

Why cdxgen + Dependency-Track

Open source management comes down to two essentials.

  1. Know what is inside — generating an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
  2. Continuously monitor risk — detecting vulnerabilities (CVEs) and license policy violations

cdxgen handles the first, and Dependency-Track handles the second. Both tools are free open source under the Apache-2.0 license.

item.title: 3.5 License Obligations
item.description:
Implementation phase

This clause is implemented in Phase 2: AI Extension Processes. View the full implementation roadmap

1. Clause Overview

License obligations are where the AI SBOM guide extends ISO/IEC 5230 the most. Whereas traditional open source compliance reviewed the licenses of code, in AI the review targets grow to four: the AI system’s code, model weights, datasets (including training, testing, and verification datasets), and the license of the AI system itself. Because it is common for one model to be derived from several other models, each upstream model in the Model Tree has its own license.

item.title: AI Extension Processes
item.description: This is Phase 2 of the implementation roadmap. It is the area where the AI SBOM guide extends ISO/IEC 5230 the most, and it covers license obligations (3.5), transparency obligations (3.6), and AI SBOM creation and management (3.9).

item.title: Identifying and Resolving Issues: Vulnerabilities and Licenses
item.description:
Where this page fits

Once identification has shown what you use, the next step is to resolve the issues that come out of it. There are two kinds of issues: security vulnerabilities and license obligations. This is the second procedure of the FSEC guide, and it corresponds to vulnerability detection and resolution (4.3.2) in ISO/IEC 18974 and to handling license use cases (3.3.2) in ISO/IEC 5230.

Documents produced here: vulnerability remediation records (including VEX), and response deadline criteria by severity.
